headline: High: Plandex can write/modify shared files and run shell commands, creating default-risk leakage and cascading errors when paired with dbt-core’s warehouse-facing workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes project files and uses a review-then-apply workflow, so dbt-core outputs placed in shared files could be treated as instructions. dbt-core itself has no shared-channel protections or prompt-filtering surface documented, so the pair has an indirect injection path via files. The pathway is plausible in default project workflows, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF dbt-core-generated text is written into a project file that Plandex reads
IF Plandex auto-applies changes from file content without human review
mitigations: Keep dbt artifacts in a separate directory from Plandex inputs
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Require manual review of any file-derived instructions
Add a file naming convention that excludes prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call a warehouse API, while Plandex reads filesystem content and sends context to a model provider or Plandex Cloud. If warehouse outputs or credentials land in the shared project directory, Plandex can ingest them and transmit them off-box. This is a default workflow risk, not a guaranteed leak, but the blast radius includes sensitive warehouse data.
conditions: IF warehouse extracts, logs, or credentials are stored in the Plandex project directory
IF Plandex forwards those files to a third-party model provider or Plandex Cloud
mitigations: Exclude secrets and warehouse exports from the project directory
Use a local-only model backend for sensitive runs
Redact warehouse outputs before Plandex reads them
Restrict filesystem access to a narrow working tree
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning before model upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad shell/network capabilities, while dbt-core interacts with the data warehouse and is commonly used in repo-based workflows. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git-state changes can collide, and dbt runs can be affected by Plandex rewrites. The profiles document overlapping mutable surfaces, so the conflict is real and potentially destructive.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Plandex modifies files while dbt-core is generating or applying warehouse-backed changes
mitigations: Serialize dbt and Plandex runs
Use separate branches for each agent
Lock the workspace during apply steps
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex’s review-then-apply flow can consume dbt-core outputs as authoritative project changes, and dbt-core’s warehouse-facing outputs may be transformed into code or config without independent verification. That creates a clear cascade from generated content to applied actions, with potential for incorrect SQL, broken models, or bad commits. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier between them.
conditions: IF dbt-core output is fed into Plandex planning or apply steps
IF Plandex applies changes without a separate validation step
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before apply
Run dbt compile/tests before Plandex apply
Compare generated diffs against expected schema changes
Limit Plandex to suggestion-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated semantic validation

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core is documented as touching data warehouse data, while Plandex handles project files and can send context to Plandex Cloud or a model provider. If warehouse data includes regulated records, the pair can create a retention or residency mismatch when those files are uploaded to external services. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is copied into Plandex-managed files
IF those files are transmitted to a third-party model provider or cloud service
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plandex workspaces
Use self-hosted or local inference only
Minimize retention in project files
Document data handling boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
